title: tailspin-oom-kv-cache-oncall-notes
summary: Notes and runbook draft from on-call response to a serving-runtime incident where continuous batching + KV cache interactions triggered memory growth and OOMs in a small subset of GPU workers. This file contains timeline, quick mitigations, deeper hypothesis, and a working runbook for similar future incidents.
content:
Incident title: tailspin — intermittent OOM cascade triggered by KV cache eviction race under continuous batching
Incident id (internal): INF-5472
Severity: Sev2 (customer-facing errors for ~5% of requests, degraded latency for others)
Impacted surface: hosted API text-generation endpoints served by runtime-v2 (subset of GPU pool: g4dn-style nodes), continuous batching enabled, small-model fast-paths
First detection: 2025-11-02 22:13 UTC (automated alert: worker OOM rate > 0.5% in 5m window)
Pager called: 22:15 UTC (on-call: Maya Ortiz)
User impact: increased 5xx rate (502/503) for certain routes, retry storms from SDK clients, transient token loss in streaming sessions
---
Short narrative (as-run):
- 22:13: alert fires: surge in worker restarts due to OOMs
- 22:15: on-call page; checked dashboards (OOM rate, mem usage, batch size distribution)
- 22:18: noticed correlation: OOMs concentrated on nodes running continuous-batching=true and kv-cache enabled
- 22:25: rolled traffic off the affected GPU pool to fallback pool (policy: region-fallback -> dedicated-fallback). Immediate 50% reduction in errors but latency increased for high-length requests
- 22:42: collected heap profiles, kernel logs, and kv-cache eviction traces, uploaded to INF-5472
- 23:10: root cause hypothesis: KV cache eviction was miscalculating prefix sizes during rapid batch slot churn, leading to memory accounting underflow and delayed reaping -> memory growth -> OOM when batches spiked
- 01:30 (next day): introduced temporary guard: for continuous-batching routes, limit max-batch-size to 32 and disable aggressive prefetching (feature flag: cbatch-prefetch=false). No new OOMs observed for 24h on affected pool
---
Telemetry & evidence collected:
- per-worker RSS and GPU memory traces (22:00-02:00 UTC)
- kv-cache eviction logs: eviction timestamp mismatches, occasional negative delta for "reserved_bytes" metric
- continuous-batching metrics: slot churn rate, max-batch-size histogram, time-in-queue distribution
- core dumps from 3 workers (attached to JIRA)
- flamegraphs collected from runtime process showing heavy allocation in cache management thread
- reproducer harness (internal) created that simulates many small prefix-invalidations while continuous batching tries to merge slots (see PR 4235)
---
Initial root cause (working hypothesis):
- A race between the KV cache eviction path and the batching slot reassigner. When many short requests arrive, continuous batching aggressively coalesces and reassigns slots. The cache eviction caller assumes a stable prefix size when subtracting reserved bytes, but slot reassignment can temporarily make the same prefix reference count increase after eviction accounting, leading to a window where the accounted reserved bytes is lower than actual resident memory. Under certain allocation patterns (prefetch + long kv entries), the process accumulates unaccounted memory until the allocator triggers OOM.
- Contributing factors:
  - aggressive prefetch introduced larger transient KV entries
  - recent quantization change increased per-token memory overhead for small models (deployed 10/30)
  - a GC / reaping path in cache was gated behind a slow timer (5s) to avoid contention; that timer is too coarse for high-churn workloads
---
What we tried during incident (and results):
- Immediate traffic migration to fallback pool: reduced error rate quickly but was disruptive to latency-sensitive users
- Feature-flag disable cbatch-prefetch: removed a source of big transient entries; OOMs subsided
- Reduced max-batch-size for continuous-batching routes: lowered peak allocations per worker
- Restarting individual workers: temporarily cleared memory but recurrence occurred until config changes above
---
Short-term mitigations (recommended for next time):
1) Emergency play: rollback cbatch-prefetch globally (ff: cbatch-prefetch=off) — fast and low-risk
2) Add OOM guard: when worker RSS crosses 85% of allowed mem, drain new batching slot assignments and route to fallback pool (protects from cascading OOMs)
3) Lower continuous-batching max default for small-model routes to 32 until code fix releases
4) Alert tuning: add a rule for eviction-gaps (metric: kvcache.unaccounted_bytes > X) to trigger earlier
---
Runbook draft: immediate actions for on-call (checks + commands)
- Step 0: Triage
  - Check dashboards: serving-runtime/oom-rate, kvcache.unaccounted_bytes, batch-slot-churn
  - Identify affected worker IDs and pools (query: infra/monitoring -> process-group filter)
- Step 1: Short circuit traffic (fastest):
  - Move route(s) to fallback pool: console route -> routing policy -> fallback (or API call to router: POST /routes/:id/reroute {policy: fallback})
  - If reroute not possible: scale up healthy pool quickly (vertical not recommended)
- Step 2: Toggle feature flags (if applicable):
  - cbatch-prefetch -> off (ff toggles in LaunchDarkly / internal FF service)
  - cbatch-max-size -> 32 (config override via config-service)
- Step 3: Contain memory growth on worker(s):
  - If OOMs continue, cordon / restart affected hosts after core dump collection
  - For persistent nodes, set process-level mem soft-limit with cgroups until fix deployed (temporary)
- Step 4: Collection for postmortem:
  - Collect /var/log/serving-runtime/*, kvcache eviction logs, profilers (pprof/heap), core dumps, kernel OOM logs
  - Attach artifacts to incident ticket and tag with "oom-kv-cache"
- Step 5: Communications
  - Post an incident update every 30 minutes to #incidents with short status + mitigations in place
  - If customers affected, coordinate with CS to send templated update (see communications snippets below)
---
Runbook checklist (quick):
- [ ] Identify affected pool IDs
- [ ] Reroute traffic to fallback/disable cbatch-prefetch
- [ ] Collect profiles + logs + cores
- [ ] Apply mem soft-limit if necessary
- [ ] Open follow-up bug(s) with reproduction steps
---
Long-term fixes proposed (prioritized):
- Hotfix (P0): Fix accounting bug in kv-cache eviction: ensure atomic update of reserved_bytes in same lock as prefix refcount changes. Add unit tests that simulate slot churn. (Owner: Ravi Singh, ETA: 2 weeks)
- Safety net (P1): Add an allocation-metering shim in cache to track actual resident_size vs accounted_reserved_bytes and emit early alerts. (Owner: Ellie Zhao, ETA: 3 weeks)
- Policy: Reduce cbatch-prefetch aggressiveness by default and document workload patterns where prefetch is safe (Owner: Product-hosted-api, ETA: 4 weeks)
- Resilience (P1): Implement faster reaping path when slot churn rate > threshold; lower timer from 5s -> 500ms adaptive (Owner: Serving-runtime team, ETA: 6 weeks)
- E2E tests: Add chaos test that runs continuous-batching and simulates KV invalidations at high frequency (Owner: release-engineering, ETA: 6 weeks)
---
Open questions / lines of investigation:
- Do we double-count memory used by quantized weights when prefetching small-model KV blobs? (Ravi to check allocator stats)
- Are there any other subsystems that expect reserved_bytes to be monotonic? Could fixing the atomicity break other invariants?
- Should fallback policy be automatic (route-level) when detecting unaccounted_bytes > threshold?
---
Comms snippets (for on-call use):
- Internal update (30m): "Incident INF-5472: Some workers in runtime-v2 experienced OOMs leading to increased 5xx. Traffic rerouted to fallback and feature-flag changes applied. Investigating KV cache accounting under high slot churn. ETA for full mitigation: TBD. Owner: Jordan Park / eng-sre."
- Customer-facing (short): "We're investigating intermittent errors on the text-generation API caused by a runtime memory issue. We've rerouted traffic and applied mitigations to reduce impact. We'll follow up with a detailed update once we have a root cause."
---
Action items (post-incident backlog):
- INF-5472: kv-cache accounting bug fix (Ravi) — due 2025-11-17 (in progress)
- INF-5481: add allocation-metering and alerts (Ellie) — due 2025-11-24
- CH-312: add chaos e2e for cbatch+kv invalidation (release-eng) — due 2025-12-08
- DOCS: update runbook and config defaults for cbatch-prefetch (Jordan) — due 2025-11-28
---
Notes to self / less formal:
- Observed weirdness: sometimes unaccounted_bytes metric was negative for a second — suggests integer underflow or wrong delta sign during concurrent updates. log-level=debug on eviction path will show sequences.
- Need to ensure we have deterministic reproducer; current harness is a close proxy but not exact of production traffic patterns (client SDK retry behavior matters).
- Keep the emacs-mode TODO: follow up on quantization change that shipped 10/30 — could be an enabling trigger rather than root cause
---
Appendix: useful commands (on-call quick)
- List recent OOM workers: curl -s "https://monitoring/api/query?m=oom_rate&window=10m&service=serving-runtime" | jq
- Reroute route to fallback: POST https://router/api/routes/:id/reroute {"policy":"fallback"}
- Toggle FF: POST https://ffsvc/api/flags/cbatch-prefetch {"value":false}
- Collect heap profile: ssh host && sudo pprof --binary=/opt/serving-runtime/bin/runtime -http=:6060 heap > /tmp/heap.pprof
---
End of notes. This is a working draft — please add discovered artifacts and edit runbook steps for clarity.
Unresolved: propagate mem soft-limit patterns to dedicated/private deployments? Needs policy discussion with product.
